patient_information: A 29-year-old married woman from Malawi, a housewife with four children, resides in a grass-thatched mud-hut in a poor rural village with an imbalanced diet.
chief_complaint: The patient presented with confusion, restlessness, and irritability for the past month, and watery diarrhoea which started one week ago.
history_of_present_illness: The patient has been confused, restless, and irritable for the past month, and has had watery diarrhoea for one week; she does not have a fever. Her past medical history was uneventful, with no psychiatric disorders, and her HIV status was unknown. She is not taking any medication and denies intoxicants.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient lives in a grass-thatched mud-hut, collects water from a borehole, has no electricity, and eats two meals a day, mainly maize porridge with few vegetables, rarely affording fish or meat.
vitals: The patient's Glasgow Coma Scale was 14/15 (confusion), the remaining vital signs were normal, and she was afebrile.
physical_exam: The patient was slim but not wasted, had pale conjunctivae, and a noticeable hyperpigmented, dry, scaly, and clearly demarcated skin rash on her neck, forearms, hands, and feet, which had been present for 2 months.
labs_and_diagnostics: An HIV test came back negative; a full blood count showed microcytic anaemia with a haemoglobin of 6.7 g/dL and a Mentzer index >13.
differential_diagnosis: Pellagra was the suspected diagnosis, with HIV infection (tuberculous meningitis, cryptococcal meningitis, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder) and systemic lupus erythematosus as differential diagnoses.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient received vitamin B-complex, iron, folic acid supplementation, a single dose of albendazole, dietary counselling, soothing applications for skin lesions, and advice to avoid sun exposure; her confusion settled within a week and diarrhoea stopped.
final_diagnosis: Pellagra, characterized by dermatitis, diarrhoea, and dementia, and microcytic anaemia were diagnosed.
